Shri Rajneesh Karnatak, MD & CEO: 
Thank you, madam. So good evening, friends. Good evening, ladies and gentlemen. 
It is a pleasure to have you with us for today’s analyst meet after the announcement 
of our Q2 FY27 financial results. Thank you for your continued interest and 
engagement with Bank of India. I look forward to sharing our quarterly performance 
and engaging with you on our progress and priorities.  
 
As we look ahead to the second half of FY27, the global environment remains 
challenging, with geopolitical conflicts, elevated crude oil prices and tighter financial 
conditions keeping inflationary pressures alive and prompting several central banks to 
raise interest rates. Against this backdrop, India has demonstrated resilience, with Q2 
GDP growth reflecting the strength of domestic demand and the economy’s firm 
underlying fundamentals. At the same time, rising inflation has prompted the RBI to 
raise the repo rate by 25 basis points, balancing price stability with the need to sustain 
growth.  
 
For banks, the opportunity now lies in translating this stability into stronger business 
growth.

My remarks today are divided into three parts. 
1. Institutional Initiatives 
 
i. 
Under our Predict-Monitor-Supervise framework, we’ve developed Star Radar – 
a predictive model that analyzes data to identify emerging risks of our branch 
network and trigger early warnings for swift intervention. 
  
ii. A dedicated Gold Loan Cell is being set up to drive robust portfolio monitoring, 
policy implementation, and direct operational support for our branches.  
 
iii. Yuva Banking Mitra will be designated at every branch to assist with youth 
account opening, promote youth-focused products, and encourage safe and 
responsible digital banking. 
 
iv. OCR- based CTS validation is being implemented as an additional alpha-
numeric layer in the Cheque Truncation System to verify cheque codes during 
clearing and bolster fraud prevention.  
 
2. Business 
i. 
Global business grew by 21.13% YoY from Rs.15.62 lakh crore in Sept’25 to 
Rs.18.92 lakh crore in Sept’26 with an incremental growth of Rs.3.30 lakh crore. 
 
ii. Global Deposits increased by 21.59% YoY from Rs. 8.53 lakh crore in Sept’25 to 
Rs. 10.37 lakh crore in Sept’26 with incremental growth of Rs. 1.84 lakh crore. 
 
iii. Domestic Deposits increased by 23.29% YoY from Rs. 7.30 lakh crore in Sept’25 
to Rs. 9.00 lakh crore in Sept’26 with incremental growth of Rs. 1.70 lakh crore. 
 
iv. CASA increased YoY from Rs. 2.86 lakh crore in Sept’25 to Rs. 3.07 lakh crore in 
Sept’26 with incremental growth of Rs. 20,539 crores and CASA ratio stood at 
34.16%. 
 
v. Global Gross Advances increased by 20.58% YoY from Rs. 7.09 lakh crore in 
Sept’25 to Rs. 8.55 lakh crore in Sept’26 with an incremental growth of Rs. 1.46 
lakh crore.
